kīnum: firm, true, steady (the adjective of kânum “to be firm”): kīnam (ki-nam, accusative) “firm”, said of ūsum “right conduct”
rīdum: leading, guidance, government (Harper’s ridu “government”, a noun of redûm “to lead”): rīdam (ri-dam, accusative) “guidance”
ṣabātum-Š: Š-stem of ṣabātum “to seize, take hold”: to make seize, make take hold: ušaṣbitu (u-ša-az-bi-tu, preterite, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause) “he made (the land) take hold”; the Š verb takes two accusatives, the one made to seize and the thing seized; the z-sign stands for ṣ
rēʾûtum: shepherdship, rule (Harper: “government, guardianship”), the abstract of rēʾûm “shepherd”: rēʾūssina (ri-u-zi-na) “their shepherding”, with the suffix -šina (t + š said ss, spelled with ZI)
-šina: their (3rd-person feminine plural possessive, on a noun): rēʾūssina “their shepherding”; after a t the š is assimilated (rēʾūt + -šina said rēʾūssina)
šulmum: peace, well-being, safety: šulmim (šu-ul-mi-im, genitive) “of peace”, and “in peace” after ina
-šināšim: for them, to them (3rd-person feminine plural dative, on a verb): ešteʾišināšim “I sought for them”, ušēṣišināšim “I brought out for them”; the accusative is -šināti
waštum: difficult, steep (Harper’s wastu): waštūtim (wa-[aš]-tu-tim, feminine plural, oblique case; the bracketed sign is Harper’s restoration) “difficult”, said of pušqum “straits”; the sense rests on Harper’s glossary alone
petûm-D: D-stem of petûm “to open”: to open up, open wide: upetti (u-[pi₂]-it-ti, preterite, 1st person singular; the bracketed sign is Harper’s restoration) “I opened up”
kakkum: weapon: kakkim (GIŠ.TUKUL, Sumerogram, no ending written; genitive after ina) “of the weapon”; Harper’s glossary gives no spelling, and the second sign (keyed TUK) is TENTATIVE
talāmum-Š: Š-stem of talāmum “to entrust” (Harper’s glossary; a rare verb): ušatlimūnim (u-ša-at-li-mu-nim) “they entrusted to me” (preterite, plural -ū, with the ventive -nim “to me”)
līʾūtum: power, might (Harper’s liʾūtu), the noun of lēʾûm “capable”: līʾūtim (li-u-tim, genitive) “of power”, after ina “with power”; līʾūti (li-u-ti) the same noun in a hard clause where the case is UNCERTAIN
elîš: above (adverb in -iš, from elûm “up”): elîš (e-li-iš); with šaplîš “below”, together “everywhere”
šaplîš: below (adverb in -iš, from šaplum “lower part”): šaplîš (ša-ap-li-iš); with elîš “above”
balûm-D: D-stem of balûm (Harper: I “to destroy”, II “to extinguish”): to put out, make an end of (Harper: “to make an end of”): ubelli (u-bi-el-li, preterite, 1st person) “I put out”
aburrum: safety, security (Harper’s aburru): aburrī (a-bu-ur-ri) “in safety”, taken as an adverb; the ending -ī is not explained by the grammar
rabāṣum-Š: Š-stem of rabāṣum “to lie down, crouch”: to make lie down, make rest (Harper: “to make to rest”): ušarbiṣ (u-šar-be-iṣ, preterite, 1st person) “I made (them) lie down”
galātum-D: D-stem of galātum (Harper’s galatu II “to molest”): mugallitam (mu-gal-li-tam, participle, accusative) “one who molests, terrifies”
-šināti: them (3rd-person feminine plural accusative, on a verb): ušaršišināti “I let them get”, attabbalšināti “I carried them”, uštapṣiršināti “I sheltered them”; the dative is -šināšim
ṣillum: shade, shelter, protection (Harper’s silu “protection”): ṣillī (ṣi-li) “my shade” (the -ī is “my”)
tarāṣum: to stretch out, spread out (Harper’s glossary): tariṣ (ta-ri-iṣ, 3rd person singular) “it is spread out”; the form’s label (stative or other) is not settled
utlum: bosom, lap, side (Harper’s utlu): utlīya (ut-li-ia) “my bosom”
nemēqum: wisdom, skill (Harper’s nemequ): nemēqīya (ne-me-qi₂-ia) “my wisdom” (KI read qi₂)
ekûtum: orphan, bereft (one) (Harper’s ekûtu), UNCERTAIN: ekûtam (NU.TUK, Sumerogram “the one who has not”, no ending written; the accusative -am is supplied)
elûm-D: D-stem of elûm “to go up”: to raise high (Harper: “to raise on high”): ullû (u-ul-lu-u, preterite, 3rd plural, in a ša-clause) “they raised high”
dīānum: judging, the giving of judgment (the infinitive of dânum “to judge”): dīānim (di-a-nim, genitive) “to judge”, after ana or without it
šūqurum: precious, weighty (Harper reads šukuru); UNCERTAIN: šūqurātim (šu-qu₂-ra-tim, feminine plural, oblique case) “weighty”, said of awātum “words”, KU read qu₂
narûm: stele, inscribed monument (Harper’s naru “monument, inscription”): narûya (na-ru-ia; also na-ru-i, with -ia “my” written short) “my stele”
ṣalmum: statue, image (Harper’s salmu): ṣalmīya (ALAN-ia) “my statue”; the sign ALAN is TENTATIVE, the word being unspelled in Harper’s glossary
watārum-Š: Š-stem of watārum “to be in excess”: to surpass, be pre-eminent (Harper’s šuturu “pre-eminent”): šūturu (šu-tu-ru) “(is) pre-eminent”, a stative
našqum: weighty, choice (Harper’s našku): našqā (na-aš-qa₂, stative plural) “(they are) weighty” (GA read qa₂)
šanānum: to rival (Harper’s šananu): šāninam (ša-ni-nam, accusative) “a rival”; the clause it stands in is UNCERTAIN
kibītum: speech, command (Harper’s kibitu): kibīt (ki-be-it, the form before a genitive) “command of”
wapûm-Št: Št-stem of wapûm “to appear”: to be made to appear, a passive sense (Harper lists it as III,2), UNCERTAIN: lištēpi (li-iš-te-bi, with li-, “let it be made to appear”; bi stands for pi₂); compare the Š-stem šūpûm “to make appear”
nazāqum-Š: Š-stem of nazāqum (Harper’s nazaku III “to cut off, efface, destroy”; the sense is not firm): to efface: mušazziqam (mu-ša-zi-qam, participle, accusative; KAM read qam) “one who effaces”, ušazziq (u-ša-zi-iq, preterite) “he effaced”; the stem and root are UNCERTAIN
ay: may not, let not (the negative-wish particle, Harper’s a “prohibitive”; written a, said ay), before a preterite: ay unakkir “may he not change”, ay ušazziq “may he not efface”, ay iršiā “may they not get”; it is not lā
zakārum-N: N-stem of zakārum “to name, mention” (Harper IV,1): passive: lizzakir (li-iz-za-ki-ir, li- + izzakir) “may it be named, be spoken of”
šaṭrum: written, inscribed (the passive participle of šaṭārum “to write”): šaṭram (ša-aṭ-ra-am, accusative) “inscribed”, said of narûm “stele”
šasûm-Gt: Gt-stem of šasûm “to call, cry out” (Harper: “to speak, tell, read”): to read aloud: lištassīma (li-iš-ta-aš-si-ma, li- + ištassi + -ma) “let him read aloud, and”
napāšum-D: D-stem of napāšum “to breathe, be at ease” (Harper’s napašu II “to set at ease”): linappišma (li-na-ab-bi-iš-ma, li- + nappiš + -ma (precative of the D); ab, bi read ap, pi₂) “let (his heart) be eased, and”; the shape and the subject (heart or man) are UNCERTAIN
irnittum: victory (Harper’s irnittu): irnitti (ir-ni-ti, the form before a genitive) “victory of”
danītum: UNCERTAIN: a solemn utterance (?) (Harper’s glossary: danitu “inscription, code”), or an adverb “firmly” from dannum “strong”; this part takes the adverb: danītam (da-ni-tam) “firmly (?)”
Zarpanītum: Zarpanitum, the consort of Marduk (goddess, with the divine determinative {d}): {d}Zar-pa-ni-tum, the first syllable one sign (Harper’s List no. 183, zar), its sign key TENTATIVE
karābum: to bless, pray (for) (Harper): likrubam (li-ik-ru-ba-am, li- + ikrub + the ventive -am “for me”) “let him pray for me”
šēdum: protective spirit, genius (Harper’s sedu “divinity”); the pair of lamassum: šēdum (še-du-um, nominative)
libittum: brick, brickwork (Harper’s libittu): libit (SIG₄, Sumerogram, form before a genitive: libit Esagila “the brickwork of Esagila”); the sign is TENTATIVE
egirrûm: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s egirru “dreams, plans”, the sense in this line unclear: igirrê (i-gi-ir-ri-e, plural, oblique case)
ūmišam: daily, each day (adverb in -išam, from ūmum “day”): ūmišam (UD-mi-ša-am)
damāqum-D: D-stem of damāqum “to be good”: to show favor, be gracious (Harper’s damaku II “to favor”): lidammiqū (li-dam-mi-qu₂, precative, 3rd plural, KU read qu₂) “may they show favor”
ṣātum: future time, eternity (Harper’s satu): ṣāt (a(=ṣa)-at, the form before a genitive; the carver wrote A for ṢA, which Harper corrects): ṣāt ūmī “the future of days”

__broaden__.ša: who, which, of · also “whose”: ša + a noun with its own suffix + the verb at the end (ša ḫaṭṭašu išarat “whose scepter is straight”), the verb in the subjunctive
__broaden__.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu) · also “over” (ana ālīya “over my city”), “before” in ana maḫar “into the presence of”; of time, ana dār “for ever”, ana warki “hereafter”, ana matīma “whenever”; ana lā + infinitive “so as not to”
__broaden__.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle” · also “with, by means of” (ina kakkim dannim “with the mighty weapon”, ina igigallim “with wisdom”), “by” with kibīt “command” and awāt “word” (the authority), “in” a manner (ina damiqtim “in favor”, ina šulmim “in peace”)
__broaden__.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye” · after a t, on a verb: uštāḫissu (uš-ta-ḫi-zu) “he has taught him” (the z of the stem + -šu said ss, spelled ZU); on nouns bīssu (É-ba/zu) “his house” and the participles murabbīšu, murabbītišu, murabbīssu “the one who raised him”; on a verb, ilqûšu, urtabbišu, urabbûšu, imtanûšu “him”; on the noun lišānšu (EME-šu) “his tongue”, īnšu “his eye”, mêšu “his waters”, mārūtišu “his sonship” · on a noun: bēlšu (be-el-šu), bēlišu (be-li-šu) “his master”, warḫušu (ITI-šu) “his month”, uznašu (u-zu-un-šu) “his ear”, nādinānšu (na-di-na-an-šu) “his seller”, nādinānišu (na-di-na-ni-šu) “his seller” after ana · written ZU in ARAD-zu, GEME₂-zu (warassu, amassu “his male slave, his female slave”) · on a verb, “him”: ukānšuma (u-ka-an-šu-ma) “he shall convict him, and” · also “its” on a Sumerogram or plural noun: GIŠ.PA-šu ḫaṭṭašu “his scepter”, SUḪUŠ-šu išdāšu “its foundations”, libbašu, libbišu “his heart”, bēlišu “his lord”, rēšīšu “its head”, dīnšu “his case”
__broaden__.-ma: and (clause-chaining particle); also “it is X that…” · “only, alone”, on a noun after ša: ša aḫḫīšama (aḫ-ḫi-ša-ma) “that of her brothers alone”; also “and” between verbs: izzazma, iššīma, išṭuršimma · also on a pronoun, “indeed” (anākuma “I indeed”), and joining chained wishes and verbs (lillikma, lišmēma, liqbīma, linappišma “… and”, ašṭurma “I wrote, and”)
__broaden__.-ia: my · written -ia after a consonant or Sumerogram (URU-ia, ALAN-ia, utlīya, narûya); the plural nouns take -ūa or -īya (awâtūa, uṣurātūa, uṣurātīya); bare -ī in ṣillī, šumī
__broaden__.kânum: to be firm; D-stem kunnum — mukīn “who makes firm” · kīnā (ki-na, stative plural) “(they) are firm”; D preterite ukīn (u-ki-in) “I/he established, set up”, ukīnūma (with the subjunctive -u and -ma) “he established, and”
__broaden__.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child” · assuḫ (az-zu-uḫ, preterite, 1st person) “I tore out”, of enemies
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere · of a tooth, to knock out: ittadi (it-ta-di, perfect) “he has knocked out”, inaddû (i-na-ad-du-u, present plural) “they shall knock out”: šinni awīlim ittadi “he has knocked out a man’s tooth” · addi (ad-di, preterite, 1st person) “I let drop”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop”, the idiom of aḫšu iddi
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate” · ittalkamma (it-ta-al-kam-ma) perfect ittalkam (ittalak + the ventive -am, “hither”) “he has come”, + -ma “and” · lillikma (li-il-li-ik-ma, li- + illik + -ma) “let him go, and”
__broaden__.egûm: to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and” · igûma (i-gu-ma) “(who) was careless, and” (the preterite igi with the relative -u, as ilqû beside ilqe, then -ma) · īgīma (i-gi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he was careless, and”: malaḫum īgīma “the boatman was careless, and” · egû (e-gu, Harper’s reading of the 1st person) “I was careless”
__broaden__.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay” · īša (i-na(=ša)) “he has”, UNCERTAIN: the carver wrote NA for ŠA and the form (īšu would be expected) is not accounted for
__broaden__.rašûm: to get, acquire: irtaši “he has acquired”, iraššû “he acquires” · iršû (ir-šu-u) “(whom) he has acquired” (the relative -u): ana mārī ša iršû “for the sons whom he has acquired” · iršiā (ir-ši-a, 3rd feminine plural preterite) after ay “may (they) not get”, with uṣurātūa as subject
__broaden__.rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN · ušaršišināti (u-šar-ši-ši-na-ti, 1st person) “I let them get”: mugallitam ul ušaršišināti “I let no molester have them”
__broaden__.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum · in broken forms …ši (ul ibašši, “there is not”, the verb itself restored); ibaššû “which are (there)”, in mimma ina qātīšu ibaššû · ibašši (i-ba-aš-ši, present) “there is, is upon”: ḫubullum elišu ibašši “a debt is upon him” · ittabši (it-tab-ši, perfect) “has happened, has broken out”, of the plague in the pen: lipit ilim ittabši “a stroke of the god has happened” · ibaššû (i-ba-aš-šu-u, present with the subjunctive -u) “who is (to the people)”
__broaden__.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma · iqabbi (written i-qa₂-ab-bi-ma, iqabbi + -ma; Harper prints the GA sign as ga, read qa₂) present “he shall say, declare”: ina maḫar ilim … iqabbima “he shall declare before the god” · liqbīma (li-iq-bi-ma, li- + iqbi + -ma) “let him say, and”
__broaden__.dīnum: case, lawsuit; judgment: dīn napištim “a case of life” · dīnāt (di-na-a-at, plural, the form before a genitive) “judgments of”; dīn mātim “the case of the land”
__broaden__.ṭâbum: to be good, pleasing; D-stem ṭubbum “make good”; muṭīb “gladdener” · ṭābu (ṭa-bu, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) is pleasing”: eliša ṭābu “it is pleasing to her” · ṭābum, ṭābam (ṭa-bu-um, ṭa-ba-am) “good”, adjective, nominative and accusative; uṭīb (u-ṭi-ib, D preterite) “I/he made good”
__broaden__.nakārum-D: D-stem of nakārum “to be strange, different”: to make different, change: uttakkir (ut-ta-ak-ki-ir, D perfect) “he has changed”: šimtam uttakkir “he has changed the mark (?)” (the object is UNCERTAIN; the verb is plain from the stem) · after ay: ay unakkir (u-na-ak-ki-ir, D preterite) “may he not change”
__broaden__.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see” · before an infinitive, ana lā ḫabālim “so as not to wrong”
__broaden__.aḫum: arm, side: aḫšu iddi “he let his arm drop” = he was idle, negligent · aḫī (a-ḫi) “my arm”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop” (aḫum + -ī “my”)
__broaden__.šâmum: to buy: ištām “he bought”, išammu “he buys” · ALSO a second verb of the same spelling, “to fix, decree” (destinies, well-being): išīm (i-ši-im) “he decreed”, išīmam (i-ši-ma-am) “he decreed for me” (preterite + the ventive -am)
__broaden__.ešērum: to be straight; Št-stem šutēšurum “to guide aright”; mušūšer · uštēšir (uš-te-še-ir, perfect) “he has set right”; šūtešurim (infinitive) “to set right”

šeʾûm: to seek (Harper): ešteʾišināšim (eš-te-i-ši-na-šim) “I have sought for them”, the G perfect (the -t- infix; 1st person singular) + the dative -šināšim; not šeʾum “grain”
paṣārum-Š: Š-stem of paṣārum (Harper: “to hide, to restrain”; his III,2 form is the perfect): to shelter, protect (UNCERTAIN: “sheltered”, “protected” and “restrained” all fit): uštapṣiršināti (uš-tap-ṣi-ir-ši-na-ti, perfect, 1st person) “I have sheltered them”, with -šināti
katātum-Š: Š-stem of a rare verb (Harper’s katatu III,2 “to give reverence to”), UNCERTAIN root: uštaktitma (uš-ta-ak-ti-it-ma, perfect, 3rd singular + -ma) “he has shown reverence, and”
matīma: whenever, at any time (Harper’s matima “at the time, when”): ana matīma (ma-ti-ma); perhaps mati “when” + -ma, UNCERTAIN
